en virkelighed.explanation: "En virkelighed" means "a reality". A very common phrase is "i virkeligheden" (in reality): "I virkeligheden er han meget genert" (In reality, he is very shy).

en virkning.explanation: "En virkning" means "an effect". With "bi-" (by) in front, it is "en bivirkning" (a side effect). To say a medicine has a side effect: "Medicinen har en bivirkning" (The medicine has a side effect).

en virksomhed.explanation: "En virksomhed" means "a business". A common word partner is "privat" (private): "en privat virksomhed" (a private business).

en virus.explanation: "En virus" means "a virus". To say you are sick because of one, use "at have" (to have): "Jeg har en virus" (I have a virus).

en vision.explanation: "En vision" means "a vision", as in a plan for the future. To talk about eyesight, use "et syn" (eyesight): "Jeg har dårligt syn" (My eyesight is bad).

en vissen blomst.explanation: "En vissen blomst" means "a withered flower". It comes from the verb "at visne" (to wither). When the thing takes "et", add "t" to "vissen": "et vissent blad" (a withered leaf).

en vitamin.explanation: "En vitamin" means "a vitamin". To name a vitamin, put the letter first: "C-vitamin" (vitamin C).

en vits.explanation: "En vits" means "a joke". The last line that makes people laugh is "en pointe" (a punchline). To say you did not get the joke: "Jeg forstod ikke pointen" (I did not get the point).

en vittighed.explanation: "En vittighed" means "a joke". It is built from "vittig" (witty) and the ending "-hed". To say someone tells a joke: "Han fortæller en vittighed" (He tells a joke).

en vogn.explanation: "En vogn" means "a wagon / cart". As the last part of a word, "vogn" is in "en indkøbsvogn" (a shopping cart): "Jeg skubber indkøbsvognen" (I push the shopping cart).

en vokal.explanation: "En vokal" means "a vowel". Danish has nine vowel letters: "a", "e", "i", "o", "u", "y", "æ", "ø" and "å".

en voksen.explanation: "En voksen" means "an adult". The word comes from "at vokse" (to grow). To say a film is for adults, use "for voksne": "en film for voksne" (a film for adults).

en vorte.explanation: "En vorte" means "a wart". To say a doctor takes it off: "Lægen fjerner vorten" (The doctor removes the wart).

en vugge.explanation: "En vugge" means "a cradle". The matching verb is "at vugge" (to rock). To say you rock a baby: "Hun vugger barnet" (She rocks the baby).

en vuggestue.explanation: "En vuggestue" means "a nursery". It is built from "en vugge" (a cradle) and "en stue" (a room). In Denmark, children go there until about three years old, then to "en børnehave" (a kindergarten): "Hun går i børnehave" (She goes to kindergarten).

en vulkan.explanation: "En vulkan" means "a volcano". To talk about an eruption, use "et vulkanudbrud" (a volcanic eruption): "Der var et vulkanudbrud på Island" (There was a volcanic eruption in Iceland).

en vurdering.explanation: "En vurdering" means "an assessment". It comes from the verb "at vurdere" (to assess). To give an estimate of what something is worth: "Vurderingen af huset er to millioner kroner" (The assessment of the house is two million kroner).

en våbenhvile.explanation: "En våbenhvile" means "a ceasefire". It is built from "et våben" (a weapon) and "en hvile" (a rest).

en vædder.explanation: "En vædder" means "a ram". The star sign Aries is "Væderen" (the Ram): "Væderen er et stjernetegn" (Aries is a star sign).

en væg.explanation: "En væg" means "a wall", as in inside a room. For a wall outdoors, such as around a garden, use "en mur" (a wall of brick or stone): "Haven har en høj mur" (The garden has a tall wall).

en vægt.explanation: "En vægt" means "a weight / a scale". To ask how heavy someone is: "Hvad er din vægt?" (What is your weight?) To talk about the machine you stand on to weigh yourself: "Vægten står på badeværelset" (The scale is in the bathroom).

en vælger.explanation: "En vælger" means "a voter". It comes from "at vælge" (to choose). To ask who someone votes for, use "at stemme" (to vote): "Hvem stemmer du på?" (Who are you voting for?)

en værdi.explanation: "En værdi" means "a value". To talk about what a person finds important, use the plural "værdier": "Vores værdier er ærlighed og frihed" (Our values are honesty and freedom).

en vært.explanation: "En vært" means "a host", as in the person who has guests. It also means the host of a show: "Hun er vært på et tv-program" (She is the host of a TV show). The word is part of "et værtshus" (a pub): "Vi mødes på værtshuset" (We meet at the pub).

en værtinde.explanation: "En værtinde" means "a hostess". It is "en vært" (a host) plus the ending "-inde", which marks a woman, as in "en veninde" (a female friend).

en værtindegave.explanation: "En værtindegave" means "a hostess gift". It is built from "en værtinde" (a hostess) and "en gave" (a gift). The part "gave" is also in "en fødselsdagsgave" (a birthday present): "Jeg købte en fødselsdagsgave" (I bought a birthday present).

en væske.explanation: "En væske" means "a liquid". To tell someone to drink plenty, use it for the fluids you drink: "Drik meget væske" (Drink a lot of fluids).

et valg.explanation: "Et valg" means "a choice". To say a decision is up to someone: "Det er dit valg" (It is your choice). When you talk about voting for a parliament or a president, it means "an election": "Der er valg i år" (There is an election this year).

et vandfald.explanation: "Et vandfald" means "a waterfall". It is built from "vand" (water) and "et fald" (a fall). To talk about a drop in numbers, "et fald" is also used: "et fald i prisen" (a fall in the price).

et vandland.explanation: "Et vandland" means "a water park". It is built from "vand" (water) and "land" (land), so literally a land of water.

et vandrerhjem.explanation: "Et vandrerhjem" means "a hostel". It is built from "en vandrer" (a hiker) and "et hjem" (a home), so literally a hiker's home. The part "hjem" is also in "et plejehjem" (a nursing home): "Min farmor bor på plejehjem" (My grandmother lives in a nursing home).

et vareudvalg.explanation: "Et vareudvalg" means "a range of goods". It is built from "en vare" (an item) and "et udvalg" (a selection). The word "et udvalg" also means a committee: "Kommunen har nedsat et udvalg" (The municipality has set up a committee).

et varsel.explanation: "Et varsel" means "a notice / warning". To talk about a weather warning: "Der er et varsel om storm i aften" (There is a storm warning tonight). To talk about advance notice at work: "Fagforeningen har givet varsel om strejke" (The union has given notice of a strike).

et vaskemærke.explanation: "Et vaskemærke" means "a care label". It is built from "vaske" (wash) and "et mærke" (a label). The word "et mærke" also means a brand: "et kendt mærke" (a famous brand).

et vaskeri.explanation: "Et vaskeri" means "a laundromat". It is built from "at vaske" (to wash) and the ending "-eri", which names a place where the work is done, as in "et bageri" (a bakery): "Vi køber brød på bageriet" (We buy bread at the bakery).

et vaskerum.explanation: "Et vaskerum" means "a laundry room". It is built from "vaske" (wash) and "et rum" (a room). The part "rum" is also in "et gæsterum" (a guest room): "Du kan sove i gæsterummet" (You can sleep in the guest room).

et vejskilt.explanation: "Et vejskilt" means "a road sign". It is built from "en vej" (a road) and "et skilt" (a sign). The word "et skilt" also works for any sign with writing: "et skilt på døren" (a sign on the door).

et vendepunkt.explanation: "Et vendepunkt" means "a turning point". It is built from "at vende" (to turn) and "et punkt" (a point). To talk about a match, use it like this: "Det var et vendepunkt i kampen" (It was a turning point in the match).

et venskab.explanation: "Et venskab" means "a friendship". It is built from "en ven" (a friend) and the ending "-skab". The same ending is in "et fællesskab" (a community): "Vi har et godt fællesskab i klassen" (We have a good community in the class).

et venteværelse.explanation: "Et venteværelse" means "a waiting room". It is built from "at vente" (to wait) and "et værelse" (a room). The part "værelse" is also in "et soveværelse" (a bedroom): "Vi har to soveværelser" (We have two bedrooms).

et verdenshav.explanation: "Et verdenshav" means "an ocean". It is built from "en verden" (a world) and "et hav" (a sea). To say you swim in the sea: "Jeg bader i havet" (I swim in the sea).

et vers.explanation: "Et vers" means "a verse". When it means poetry in general, it has no article: "Han skriver vers" (He writes poetry).

et videoopkald.explanation: "Et videoopkald" means "a video call". It is built from "video" (video) and "et opkald" (a call). To talk about an ordinary phone call, use "et opkald" alone: "et opkald fra min mor" (a call from my mom).

et vidne.explanation: "Et vidne" means "a witness". To say you saw something happen, use "at være vidne til" (to witness): "Jeg var vidne til ulykken" (I witnessed the accident). A witness is a person, but "et bevis" (a piece of evidence) is a thing: "Billedet er et bevis" (The photo is evidence).

et vidnesbyrd.explanation: "Et vidnesbyrd" means "a testimony / evidence". To name what the evidence proves, use "om" (of): "et vidnesbyrd om hendes mod" (evidence of her courage). For what a person tells the police or a court, use "et vidneudsagn" (a witness statement): "Politiet har hørt hans vidneudsagn" (The police have heard his witness statement).

et vidneudsagn.explanation: "Et vidneudsagn" means "a testimony". It is built from "et vidne" (a witness) and "et udsagn" (a statement). To talk about what someone said, use "et udsagn" alone: "Hans udsagn var forkert" (His statement was wrong).

et vilkår.explanation: "Et vilkår" means "a term", as in an agreement. To tell someone to read the conditions of a contract: "Læs vilkårene først" (Read the terms first). When you talk about the circumstances someone works under, use it in the same way: "Det er svære vilkår at arbejde under" (These are difficult circumstances to work under).

et vindue.explanation: "Et vindue" means "a window". To talk about a window on a computer screen, the same word is used: "åbn et nyt vindue" (open a new window).

et vinglas.explanation: "Et vinglas" means "a wine glass". It is built from "vin" (wine) and "et glas" (a glass). The word "glas" is also the material: "en flaske af glas" (a bottle made of glass).

et visitkort.explanation: "Et visitkort" means "a business card". The part "kort" (card) is also in "et kreditkort" (a credit card): "Jeg betaler med kreditkort" (I pay with a credit card).

et viskelæder.explanation: "Et viskelæder" means "an eraser". It is built from "at viske" (to wipe) and "et læder" (leather). The word "læder" is also the material itself: "en jakke af læder" (a jacket made of leather).

et viskestykke.explanation: "Et viskestykke" means "a dish towel". It is built from "at viske" (to wipe) and "et stykke" (a piece). The word "et stykke" also works for a piece of food: "et stykke kage" (a piece of cake).

et visum.explanation: "Et visum" means "a visa". To say you have applied for one, use "at søge om" (to apply for): "Jeg har søgt om visum" (I have applied for a visa).

et våben.explanation: "Et våben" means "a weapon". To use the word for something that is not physical: "Humor er et våben" (Humor is a weapon).

et vådområde.explanation: "Et vådområde" means "a wetland". It is built from "våd" (wet) and "et område" (an area). The word "et område" also works on its own: "Området er lukket" (The area is closed).

et væddemål.explanation: "Et væddemål" means "a bet". To say you bet on something, use the verb "at vædde" (to bet): "Jeg vil vædde på, at han kommer for sent" (I bet he will be late).

et vækkeur.explanation: "Et vækkeur" means "an alarm clock". It is built from "at vække" (to wake someone) and "et ur" (a clock). To ask someone to wake you: "Kan du vække mig i morgen?" (Can you wake me tomorrow?)

et værelse.explanation: "Et værelse" means "a room", as in a room in a home or hotel. For room in the sense of free space, use "plads" (space): "Der er plads" (There is room).

et værk.explanation: "Et værk" means "a work", as in a work of art: "Det er et af hans bedste værker" (It is one of his best works). To talk about a factory-like place, it is also the last part of words such as "et stålværk" (a steel mill): "Han arbejder på et stålværk" (He works at a steel mill).

et værksted.explanation: "Et værksted" means "a workshop, a garage". It is built from "et værk" (a work) and "et sted" (a place). For a garage where you park, use "en garage" (a garage): "Bilen står i garagen" (The car is in the garage).

et værktøj.explanation: "Et værktøj" means "a tool". When you talk about tools in general, leave out "et": "Jeg har værktøj i skuret" (I have tools in the shed).

et værn.explanation: "Et værn" means "a defense". To talk about protection against harm: "et værn mod kriminalitet" (a safeguard against crime). To name a part of the armed forces: "Hæren er et af værnene" (The army is one of the branches).

et værtshus.explanation: "Et værtshus" means "a pub". It is built from "en vært" (a host or landlord) and "et hus" (a house). The word "hus" also works on its own: "Vi bor i et stort hus" (We live in a big house).

et væsen.explanation: "Et væsen" means "a creature / being". To talk about a person's nature, it means "manner": "Hun har et roligt væsen" (She has a calm manner).

et væv.explanation: "Et væv" means "a tissue". It comes from the verb "at væve" (to weave). The same word is the last part of "et spindelvæv" (a spider web): "Der hænger et spindelvæv i hjørnet" (A spider web hangs in the corner).

vand.explanation: "Vand" means "water". It has no article when you talk about water in general: "Jeg drikker vand" (I drink water). To order a drink, use "et glas" (a glass): "Et glas vand, tak" (A glass of water, please).

vanilje.explanation: "Vanilje" means "vanilla". It is the first part of food words such as "vaniljeis" (vanilla ice cream): "Jeg vil have en kugle vaniljeis" (I would like a scoop of vanilla ice cream).

vanskelig.explanation: "Vanskelig" means "difficult". A word with the same meaning is "svær" (hard): "Opgaven er svær" (The task is hard). When the thing takes "et", add "t" to "vanskelig": "et vanskeligt spørgsmål" (a difficult question).

vant til.explanation: "Vant til" means "used to", as in being accustomed to something: "Jeg er vant til kulden" (I am used to the cold). For a past habit, use "plejede at" (used to): "Jeg plejede at bo i Aarhus" (I used to live in Aarhus).

vanvid.explanation: "Et vanvid" means "a madness". To say an idea is reckless: "Det er vanvid at køre så hurtigt" (It is madness to drive that fast).

vanvittig.explanation: "Vanvittig" means "crazy". To describe an idea: "en vanvittig idé" (a crazy idea). Before another describing word it means "extremely": "Det er vanvittigt dyrt" (It is insanely expensive).

varetægt.explanation: "En varetægt" means "custody", as in "i politiets varetægt" (in police custody). For custody of a child, use "forældremyndighed" (parental custody) instead: "Hun har forældremyndigheden over børnene" (She has custody of the children).

varig.explanation: "Varig" means "lasting". It comes from the verb "at vare" (to last). When the thing takes "et", add "t" to "varig": "et varigt mén" (a lasting injury).

varm.explanation: "Varm" means "warm". To say a drink or food is hot, the same word is used: "varm kaffe" (hot coffee). When the thing takes "et", add "t": "et varmt hus" (a warm house).

varme.explanation: "En varme" means "heat / warmth". To heat something up, use the verb "at varme" (to heat): "Jeg varmer suppen" (I am heating the soup). When it describes more than one thing, "varme" means "warm": "varme dage" (warm days).

varsom.explanation: "Varsom" means "cautious". To say what you are careful with, add "med" (with): "at være varsom med sine ord" (to choose your words with care).

vaskepulver.explanation: "Vaskepulver" means "laundry detergent". It is built from "at vaske" (to wash) and "et pulver" (a powder). The word for any kind of detergent, powder or liquid, is "et vaskemiddel" (a detergent): "Vaskemidlet står på hylden" (The detergent is on the shelf).

vasketøj.explanation: "Vasketøj" means "laundry". It is built from "at vaske" (to wash) and "tøj" (clothes). To say you have a lot of laundry, use no article before "vasketøj": "Jeg har meget vasketøj" (I have a lot of laundry).

ved.explanation: "Ved" means "by". To say where someone sits next to something: "Han sidder ved vinduet" (He sits by the window). When you talk about a table or desk where someone sits or works, it means "at": "Vi sidder ved bordet" (We sit at the table). The same spelling is also a form of "at vide" (to know): "Jeg ved det" (I know it).

ved siden af.explanation: "Ved siden af" means "next to". It is built from "ved" (by), "siden" (the side) and "af" (of), so literally by the side of. To say you do something in addition to a job: "Jeg læser ved siden af mit arbejde" (I study alongside my job).

vedholdenhed.explanation: "En vedholdenhed" means "a persistence". To say that a task needs it: "Det kræver vedholdenhed at skrive en bog" (It takes persistence to write a book). For the strength of your body, use "udholdenhed" (stamina): "Maratonløbere har stor udholdenhed" (Marathon runners have great stamina).

vedkommende.explanation: "Vedkommende" means "the person". To talk about a person without saying "han" (he) or "hun" (she): "Vedkommende har ikke svaret" (The person has not answered).

vedligeholdelse.explanation: "Vedligeholdelse" means "maintenance". To talk about fixing something that is already broken, use "en reparation" (a repair): "Bilen skal til reparation" (The car needs repair).

vedrørende.explanation: "Vedrørende" means "regarding". To name the subject of a letter or email, write it first: "Vedrørende din bestilling" (Regarding your order). It is shortened to "vedr." in writing.

vedvarende.explanation: "Vedvarende" means "persistent". It comes from "at vare" (to last). In "vedvarende energi" it means "renewable".

vedvarende energi.explanation: "Vedvarende energi" means "renewable energy". It is "vedvarende" (lasting) and "energi" (energy), so literally lasting energy.

vegansk.explanation: "Vegansk" means "vegan". To talk about a person who eats this way, use "en veganer" (a vegan): "Min søster er veganer" (My sister is a vegan).

vegetarisk.explanation: "Vegetarisk" means "vegetarian". To ask a restaurant for food without meat: "Har I noget vegetarisk?" (Do you have anything vegetarian?) To talk about a person who eats this way, use "en vegetar" (a vegetarian): "Min bror er vegetar" (My brother is a vegetarian).

vejarbejde.explanation: "Vejarbejde" means "roadworks". It is built from "en vej" (a road) and "et arbejde" (a job). To warn about a road: "Der er vejarbejde på motorvejen" (There are roadworks on the highway).

vejr.explanation: "Vejr" means "weather". To ask what it is like outside: "Hvordan er vejret?" (How is the weather?) The same word is also in "at trække vejret" (to breathe), where it means "the breath": "Jeg kan ikke trække vejret" (I cannot breathe).

vejrtrækning.explanation: "En vejrtrækning" means "a breath / breathing". It is built on "at trække vejret" (to take a breath), where "vejret" means "the breath" here, not the weather. To say you hold your breath: "Jeg holder vejret" (I am holding my breath).

vel.explanation: "Vel" means "I suppose". To say you guess that something is fine: "Det er vel i orden" (I suppose that is fine). To ask a question where you expect the answer no: "Han er vel ikke gået?" (He has not left, has he?)

velbegrundet.explanation: "Velbegrundet" means "well-founded". It is built from "vel" (well) and "begrundet" (given reasons for).

velbekomme.explanation: "Velbekomme" means "Enjoy! / You're welcome!". When you put food in front of someone, say it: "Velbekomme!" (Enjoy!) When someone thanks you for a meal, say it back: "Tak for en dejlig middag." "Velbekomme." (Thanks for a lovely dinner. You're welcome.) For other thanks, say "selv tak" (you're welcome): "Tak for hjælpen." "Selv tak." (Thanks for the help. You're welcome.)

veldrevet.explanation: "Veldrevet" means "well-run". It is built from "vel" (well) and "at drive" (to run), as in "en veldrevet butik" (a well-run shop). For a place that looks neat and cared for, use "velholdt" (well-kept): "et velholdt hus" (a well-kept house).

velfortjent.explanation: "Velfortjent" means "well-deserved". It is built from "vel" (well) and "at fortjene" (to deserve). The opposite is "ufortjent" (undeserved): "Det var en ufortjent sejr" (It was an undeserved win).

velfærd.explanation: "Velfærd" means "welfare". In Denmark it especially means public services paid for by taxes, such as health care, schools and care for the old. A country that provides them is "en velfærdsstat" (a welfare state): "Danmark er en velfærdsstat" (Denmark is a welfare state).

velfærdssamfundet.explanation: "Et velfærdssamfund" means "a welfare society". It is built from "velfærd" (welfare) and "et samfund" (a society). In Denmark, taxes pay for things such as schools and health care.

velgørenhed.explanation: "Velgørenhed" means "charity". For a charity as an organization, use "en velgørenhedsorganisation" (a charity organization): "Jeg giver penge til en velgørenhedsorganisation" (I give money to a charity organization).

velhavende.explanation: "Velhavende" means "wealthy". It is built from "vel" (well) and "at have" (to have). A shorter word with the same meaning is "rig" (rich): "Han er rig" (He is rich).
